description: The bar chart titled “Evaluation Based on Different Tasks” visually compares the accuracy of three model variants—“Base,” “RMU with Enhanced GCG,” and “RMU”—across two distinct evaluation tasks: “MCQ Eval” and “Generation Eval.” The vertical y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.6 in increments of 0.2, with tick marks at 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, and 0.6. The horizontal x-axis displays the two evaluation categories: “MCQ Eval” on the left and “Generation Eval” on the right. For “MCQ Eval,” the “Base” model (reddish-brown bar) achieves an accuracy of 0.644, the “RMU with Enhanced GCG” model (light green bar) scores 0.539, and the “RMU” model (beige bar) scores 0.299. For “Generation Eval,” the “Base” model again leads with 0.597, followed by “RMU with Enhanced GCG” at 0.263, and “RMU” at 0.106. A legend beneath the chart identifies the color coding for each model variant. The chart uses grouped vertical bars for each evaluation task, with each group containing three bars representing the three models. The “Base” model consistently outperforms the other two across both tasks, and the “RMU” model shows the lowest accuracy in both cases. No error bars or statistical significance indicators are present, and the bars are not sorted by height within groups — they are ordered consistently by model type as defined in the legend. The overall visual design is minimal, with no gridlines or background shading beyond the axis labels and title.
